title: Kollar's lemma: a Noetherian local ring is Artinian, regular of dimension one, of depth at least two, or has a finite birational-type extension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring. Consider the four properties: (1) $R$ is Artinian (every descending chain of ideals of $R$ is stationary); (2) $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; (3) $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]; (4) there is a ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$ to a nonzero commutative ring $R'$ such that $R'$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module through $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $\varphi$ is not an isomorphism, there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^n\cdot\ker(\varphi)=0$ and $\mathfrak m^n R'\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of the $R$-module $R'$, i.e. there is no $z\in R'$ whose annihilator $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}$ equals $\mathfrak m$. Then (i) at least one of (1)-(4) holds, and (ii) (3) and (4) do not hold together.

proof.text: Split on whether R is Artinian. In the non-Artinian case use Mathlib isArtinianRing_iff_isNilpotent_maximalIdeal and stabilize the increasing colon ideals Ann(m^n) by monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian. If m is associated to R, the stabilized ideal J is nonzero and proper, m^n J = 0, and m is not associated to R/J. These facts are proved directly in torsion_quotient. The quotient map, composed with a universe lift, gives the extension alternative; all finite, non-bijective, annihilation and associated-prime conditions are checked in extension_of_torsion_quotient.

If m is not associated to R, apply exists_mem_maximalIdeal_smul_injective to get a regular x in m. If m is associated to QuotSMulTop x R, apply the regular-element alternatives. Otherwise apply the same nonzerodivisor lemma to QuotSMulTop x R to obtain y in m. Mathlib regular-sequence cons and singleton lemmas show [x,y] is weakly regular; membership in m makes it regular. Its length two is an element of the supremum defining depth, so depth is at least two.

For exclusion assume depth R >= 2 and an extension phi with exponent n. Positive depth supplies a first regular element in m: otherwise every regular sequence contributing to the depth supremum would be empty. A power of this element annihilates the kernel by m^n ker phi = 0; regularity of powers proves the kernel is zero, hence phi injective.

The absence of an element of S with annihilator m translates by isAssociatedPrime_iff to m not in associatedPrimes R S. Obtain a regular element in m on S and hence depth S >= 1 from its singleton sequence. If Q = S/range(phi) is nonzero, the depth lemma for the exact sequence R -> S -> Q gives depth Q >= min(depth S, depth R - 1) >= 1. Obtain a regular element in m on Q. The image-ideal hypothesis implies m^n Q = 0. Its nth power is both regular and zero on Q, so Q is subsingleton, contradiction. Therefore phi is surjective; with injectivity this contradicts non-bijectivity.

lean.statement: theorem kollar_local_dichotomy (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] : let extension : Prop := ∃ (S : Type (max u v)) (sRing : CommRing S), letI := sRing ∃ φ : R →+* S, letI := φ.toAlgebra Nontrivial S ∧ Module.Finite R S ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective φ ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n * RingHom.ker φ = ⊥ ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ideal.map φ ((maximalIdeal R) ^ n), z ∈ φ.range) ∧ ¬ ∃ z : S, ∀ a : R, φ a * z = 0 ↔ a ∈ maximalIdeal R (IsArtinianRing R ∨ (IsRegularLocalRing R ∧ ringKrullDim R = 1) ∨ (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) R ∨ extension) ∧ ¬ ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) R ∧ extension)
